objects.name: Patch (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
An area of the section filled with fibres - one fibre per mesh face, at its centroid.
Mesh in m, so fibre areas come out in m2.

objects.name: Fiber Section (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Collects fibre points, layers and patches into one section.
The green y and blue z arrows are the section's local axes: y along world X, z along world Y, the way OpenSees writes a fibre. They are drawn at the area centroid of the fibres, the point moments are taken about. My and Mz - in Moment Curvature, Interaction Domain and its views - are moments about y and z by the right-hand rule, the beam's axis x coming out of the drawing (towards you in Top view): positive My stretches the +z side, positive Mz the -y side.

objects.name: ForceBeamColumn (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc: Construct a beam element. Switch between a standard ForceBeamColumn (Beam), a beam with plastic hinge zones (WithHinges) and a bar that carries axial force only (Truss).

objects.name: Spring Link (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
A spring between two nodes that are apart - a bearing, a bolt, a damper, the interlayer of a laminate.
One material per direction, and only the directions given carry anything: a link on direction 1 alone pulls along its own axis and resists nothing else.
Directions are local. 1 runs along the link, 2 and 3 across it, unless a Plane says otherwise.
For a join with no give at all use a Rigid Link, which is exact and needs no stiffness.

objects.name: Support (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
A support. Rigid: fixes the node along and about the axes of the Position's plane you choose. Elastic: a spring along or about each axis of the plane. Compression Only: holds the node only while it pushes into the support, along the plane's Z, and lets it lift - after a gap, if there is one.
Elastic and Compression Only never fix the node themselves, so a Rigid support on the same point can hold what they leave free: a pinned bearing that can lift is a Compression Only support with a Rigid one holding Tx and Ty only.
Reaction Force gives a spring support a row of its own, with the spring's force.

objects.name: Gravity Load (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc: Construct a Gravity Load: the model's own weight, down. A beam carries its weight as a uniform load along it, a truss half on each end, a shell or a solid shared among its nodes.

objects.name: Pushover Analysis (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Pushes the model sideways until it gives way: the capacity curve, base shear against the displacement of a control point.
The loads of the assembled model - its self-weight, its floors - are applied first and held. Then the lateral loads are scaled up, step by step, until the control point has moved Target along Direction. The push is controlled by that displacement, not by the load, so it goes on past the peak, where the structure softens.
For the beams to yield, give them fibre sections (Fiber Section, MomentCurvature tab) on ForceBeamColumn: an elastic section stays elastic, and its curve is a straight line. With P-Delta on, the loads the columns carry push them further as the frame sways.
Feed the pushed model to Model View or to the result components with a Step from the Step output to see any point of the curve.

objects.name: Model View (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Draw the model and its results in the viewport.
Tick one or more results under Results - displacements, beam forces and stresses, shell forces and stresses, solid stresses, reactions - to draw them together, each with its own component and unit. Under Beam forces, tick any of N, Vy, Vz, T, My and Mz to draw their diagrams together. They need a model from Run Analysis or another analysis. Each element is coloured by one result: an element's own stress or force before the displacement, which colours the rest.
With none ticked, the elements are coloured by element, section or material.
Node and element ids, section names, local axes, end releases, loads and supports can be drawn over either, from the Elements, Loads and Supports menus.
ElementId shows only some of the elements and greys the rest, so what you are looking at stays in the model around it.
Geometry hands out what is drawn as coloured meshes and lines - move it, or bake it.
With Extruded on, beam stresses that differ across a section - σx, σMy, σMz, τV, τT, Von Mises - are painted point by point over it; drawn as lines, each section shows its worst.
A vibration or buckling mode is drawn at deformation scale 1 with its largest movement as far off the model as the diagrams stand; any other displacement at true size. On a natural vibration or buckling model the scale runs from -2 to 2, so Animate swings the mode both ways.
While Animate runs, the colours grow with the deformation: the model at rest is all the colour of zero, and at the full swing it shows the result's own colours. The Legend and the values written stay as they are.

objects.name: Group
objects.nick: 2 - Planks: birch plywood as Steel01, in fibres, on Corotational ForceBeamColumns

objects.name: Group
objects.nick: 3 - Bolts and feet: a Spring Link a crossing, free to turn about the bolt; the feet pinned

objects.name: Group
objects.nick: 4 - Loads: its own weight, held; the push, its weight again at every node

objects.name: Group
objects.nick: 5 - Pushover: the crown pushed to Push to mm, down (Z) or sideways (X, Y)

objects.name: Panel
objects.desc: A panel for custom notes and text values
objects.text:
Reciprocal vault - plywood planks bolted where they cross, pressed down until the vault gives way.

A barrel vault 4 m across, 2 m high and 4.8 m long, of planks 127 x 18 mm in a pinwheel pattern: round each node of a grid four planks turn about a small opening, each resting on the next, one bolt at each crossing. The planks are moved until every crossing is one plank deep. Each plank is a chain of ForceBeamColumns between its bolts, on a Fiber Section of Steel01 standing in for birch plywood - 9 000 MPa, yielding at 25 MPa - with Corotational transformations, as the vault moves far before it gives way. Each bolt is a Spring Link 18 mm long: 4 000 kN/m across it, free to turn about it. The feet are pinned.

Pushover Analysis holds its own weight, then adds its weight again, a share at every node, and scales it until the crown has moved Push to mm: down for Direction Z, sideways for Y or X. The curve reads in times its own weight pressed down, or in g sideways. Point on the curve picks a point of it; Model View draws the vault there, as it is, with a ball where the plywood has yielded, coloured by how far: yellow from first yield, orange from twice its yield strain, red from four times, dark red from eight; faded once it has unloaded. A ball stays once it has come.

What it shows: pressed down, the vault carries its own weight and 2.4 times as much again, its crown 220 mm down, then gives way, the crown dropping as the load falls off. The first plastic hinge forms at 1.5 times; 104 have by the end. Pushed sideways, it does not give way: it leans further and further and stiffens, its planks pulled into a net.

Not in it: plywood breaking. Steel01 yields in tension as in compression, where a plank of plywood would crack: the first Hinges, at about 1.5 times its weight, are where a real one would start to. Nor the play in the bolt holes, the planks crushing round the bolts, a bolt tearing out. Its bolts never slip and never break, so the vault is stiffer, and stronger, than one built.

Try: Direction Y, and Push to 1000 mm; Plank thickness 24 mm; Fan wider.
